title: The Head Of GTA 6’s Parent Company Helped Make One Of The Best Christmas Movies Of All Time
text:
One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market.

Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32.

Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein.

Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone.

That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part.

So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies?

Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO.

"I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview.

After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997.

After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud.

Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter. Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.

title: WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.

Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back.

Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies.

Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group.

As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14.

"With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard said in a forum post. 

At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends.

It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. 

Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic.

Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.

title: GTA 6 Should Help Boost PS5 And Xbox Sales, But Their Astronomical Prices Could Hurt
text:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why.

According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella said anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a new console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today.

Historical prices

When GTA 5 launched in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today.

"Not a good thing"

Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the company launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console.

 "However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands," he said. "Probably the most relevant thing is the world continues to move to open systems, and that will continue.”

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in New Zealand get to play first, and if you're planning a trip to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for safely packing your PS5.

title: EA Begs You To Not Delete Madden 27 For GTA 6
text:
We all know what's coming: Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether you're ready for it or not, the most anticipated game of the decade is preparing to launch on November 19, and ahead of its release, EA is begging you to please not ditch footballs for guns.

According to Push Square, EA added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27. The pop-up says there's an update coming to the football simulator on November 17, just before GTA 6 drops.

"Don't delete," the message reads. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17 ... do not leak this transmission!"

In a November 10 post on Madden NFL 27's official X account, EA said that a throwback Madden 97 update is coming on November 18 with old-school playbooks, 16-bit gameplay, and the All '97 Team. Underneath that post, EA had asked that you stick around a little while longer.

This is in reference to the humongous amount of storage space that Rockstar Games' GTA 6 will take up when it launches. Start clearing out your hard drive now because you need at least 212GB of free space to download GTA 6. In comparison, Madden NFL 27 needs approximately 60GB to install the game.

If you're like me and you still have the base PS5, this means you have approximately 667GB of usable space. Sure, you can fit both GTA 6 and Madden NFL 27 on the same console. However, if you have any other recent releases like The Blood of Dawnwalker (~50GB), Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen (~81GB), Phantom Blade Zero (~135GB), and Valor Mortis (~60GB), then you can see how quickly you'll run out of space--especially since you have to leave a little wiggle room for game updates, too. That's not to mention the games dropping in 2027, such as Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which game director Naoki Hamaguchi said could be around 200GB.

EA has recently gone through a restructuring that saw 400 employees across the company get let go and the legendary studio BioWare get shut down. In the midst of this, the publisher reiterated its commitment to the Madden franchise with a new title currently codenamed Project Gridiron. While filled with potential, we do fear that EA's plan for the series may lean into everything that the company itself does wrong.

title: Rockstar Could Have Released GTA 6 Sooner As GTA 5.5, But “You Have To Take Big Swings”
text:
After years of development, multiple delays, and loads of hype, Rockstar Games is finally releasing Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19. What took so long?

According to Rockstar publishing executive Jennifer Kolbe, the team at Rockstar "could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster." However, "Ultimately, that's not what they wanted," she told The Guardian.

Rockstar boss Rob Nelson, meanwhile, said it was important for the studio to go above and beyond with GTA 6, and that takes time. "You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same," he said.

GTA 6 looks to be a big step up from GTA 5 in a number of ways, including the visuals and technical improvements. Beyond that, the story this time around is a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style narrative about a crime-loving couple--Jason and Lucia. It's also the first time Rockstar is releasing a GTA game with a playable female protagonist.

GTA 6 took so long to come out because Rockstar is seeking "perfection," according to Take-Two. “The team at Rockstar really does seek to do something that’s never been done before. That’s really hard and it takes a long time,” he said.

Rockstar and its owner, Take-Two, stand to benefit greatly from what's expected to be a commercial blockbuster with GTA 6. But could future GTA game releases come at a faster pace? According to Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will look "dramatically different" over the next decade, but he didn't share more or commit to any specific timelines.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia can attend a funeral at KFC to get the day off work to play it.

GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

title: Shooting Suspect In Custody After Opening Fire Near Xbox Dev’s Studio
text:
A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect.

Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting.

"Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson said. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation.

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Currently, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

title: We Got A Grand Theft At Disney World Before GTA 6
text:
The "We got X before GTA 6" meme continues as a Grand Theft has been reported at Walt Disney World's Epcot theme park just days before Rockstar's open-world crime game releases, and the meme comes to an end.

The Walt Disney World: Active Calls account, which tracks police reports in the Disney World area, said a Grand Theft call at Epcot came in at 9:52 PM on November 14.

There are no further details to go on here, but Grand Theft, known as Grand Larceny in some states, involves stealing something valuable. Epcot and Disney in general has lots of items that would be considered valuable.

This is the closest that Disney World might come to GTA 6, as Rockstar already confirmed that GTA 6 won't have its own version of the park. That makes sense, too, considering Walt Disney World is located in Orlando and GTA 6 takes place in its own version of Miami, which is more than 200 miles away.

Calls for Grand Theft are not uncommon at Disney World. In October 2026 alone, the County Sheriff's Office received at least seven Grand Theft calls.

One of the most infamous heists at Walt Disney World took place at Epcot. In 2018, thieves nabbed the multi-hundred-pound Buzzy animatronic from the Cranium Command attraction, which was housed at Epcot's shuttered Wonders of Life pavilion.

It has never been recovered. A documentary, Stolen Kingdom, was released in 2025, chronicling the heist and the wider black market for Disney props.

More recently, the Paddlefish restaurant at the Disney World entertainment district, Disney Springs, was robbed by someone who swam up to the waterside restaurant in frogman gear, forced two workers into a corner, obscured the security camera with foam, and made off with cash. This case has not been solved.

In other Disney news, the entertainment giant is teasing "major" announcements for The Game Awards next month. As for GTA 6, the game finally releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

The "We got X before GTA 6" memes have been among the most popular and hilarious over the years as fans waited and waited for the game to release. Even Take-Two's own CEO, Strauss Zelnick, is aware of the memes.

title: GTA 6 Promo At KFC Is A Fake Funeral So You Can Take The Day Off To Play
text:
The popular fried chicken chain KFC has announced a frankly absurd GTA 6 promotion: a fake funeral so people have a “legitimate” excuse to take the day off to play Rockstar’s latest.

The fake funeral for a woman, "Ann Alibi," will take place Thursday, November 19 at 11 AM at KFC Robina in Queensland. People can attend in person or watch the funeral by livestream. The local restaurant is part of a region of Australia known as the Gold Coast, which KFC says is the equivalent of GTA 6's Vice City (which itself is a stand-in for Miami).

"The service will include a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest. All the appropriate arrangements for a fitting farewell," KFC said.

The restaurant is also handing out free fried chicken to anyone who shows up in person. For those who can't make the services, KFC will offer free delivery through its app across Australia on November 19.

Anyone planning to eat fried food and play video games should be mindful of what might happen to their controller ... unless you got your hands on the limited-edition "greaseproof" controller that Microsoft put out years ago. Check out the video below to see how an Xbox controller holds up to heavy grease.

A KFC spokesperson said of the GTA 6 promo, "We appreciate that Australians have responsibilities, but some occasions are simply too important to miss. And in accordance with Ann's final wishes, we've made sure the funeral takes place during working hours."

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia will be among the first in the world to play it since the game unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play GTA 6.

title: Xbox Is Looking For Smarter Ways To Stop Its Next Console From Costing A Fortune
text:
No one knows yet exactly what the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix, will be, but most people are convinced it won't be cheap. The ongoing memory shortage has driven current-gen console prices skyward since 2024, with the Xbox Series X rising from $500 in 2020 to $800 in 2026. Project Helix is projected to cost as much as $1,800 at launch, but Microsoft aims to keep the price down when it eventually releases the device.

According to VP of next-gen Jason Ronald, techniques like neural rendering could help manage costs. "It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable," Ronald said in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine. "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

In a nutshell, neural rendering uses AI to predict and generate high-quality video game frames while using only a portion of hardware power, similar to upscaling technoligies like PSSR, DLSS, and FSR. This could enable next-generation visual leaps while keeping the console accessible and reasonably priced for consumers. The other benefit is that the AI software models can improve over time through updates, as console hardware remains fixed over its lifespan, hence Ronald's quote about improvements reaching Project Helix over a few years into its run.

It remains to be seen how these breakthroughs will be spread across Project Helix, which Ronald teased as a family of devices that can address home, mobile, and cloud gaming needs. Xbox suggesting that it's working smarter to deliver an affordable gaming experience is an idea that Shawn Layden touched on recently, as the former PlayStation boss spoke about how Sony should be less concerned with chasing improved graphics and rather focus on making a cheaper PS5-level console instead.

Meanwhile, Sony is squeezing more life out of the PS5 generation with AI-guided upscaling technology, and the base model PS5 got its own version of this in the form of Quick Spectral Super Resolution. Originally available for only two games, QSSR is coming to more titles in the future, like Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and No Man's Sky.

title: GTA 6 Nearing 15 Million Copies Sold And $1.5 Billion In Revenue, And The Game Isn’t Even Out Yet
text:
The video game research company Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker to reveal the latest, albeit unofficial, sales data for the open-world crime game. According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has now sold 14.94 million total units via pre-purchases, which works out to about $1.45 billion in gross revenue.

The report said PS5 sales are dominating the mix, with GTA 6 selling 11.13 million units on PS5 so far, compared to 3.81 million on Xbox Series X|S. That means of the 14.94 million GTA 6 sales so far, 74% are on PS5 and 26% on Xbox Series X|S.

In total, GTA 6 sales for PS5 have so far reached $1.08 billion in revenue, compared to $3.81 million for Xbox Series X|S. Sony and Microsoft keep about 30% of revenue due to their platform fees, so GTA 6 being a huge success directly benefits both of those companies.

The huge gap in sales between platforms is not surprising because the PS5 is dominating Xbox Series X|S in terms of console sales. In fact, GTA 6 is breaking records on Xbox, Microsoft has said, and the sales numbers for GTA 6 on Xbox line up with Xbox's share of the console market.

Sensor Tower is projecting as many as 25 million total pre-purchases for GTA 6 by launch, and if the 75/25 split holds, that would be about 18.5 million units on PS5 and 6.5 million on Xbox Series X|S.

GTA 6 is the most preordered game of all time for PlayStation and Xbox. If the 10 million pre-purchase number is real, that would break a record for most preorders set by Cyberpunk 2077 (8 million).

Sony holds the marketing rights for GTA 6 on PS5, but that doesn't mean that Microsoft is doing nothing to try to promote the game. Just recently, Microsoft announced a GTA 6-inspired custom Xbox console that sits inside an alligator.

Circana has released new data that shows that GTA 6 holds 29% purchase intent among US console and PC gamers. That means nearly 1 in 3 console and PC gamers in the US plan to buy GTA 6–this is the highest purchase intent that Circana has ever measured for any game.

GTA 6 may indeed be a gigantic hit commercially, and one that helps lift the entire industry with increased sales of hardware and accessories. But anyone looking to buy a new console to play GTA 6 is set for major sticker shock, as consoles today are more expensive than ever. Not only that, but GTA 6 is not going to save the industry’s many serious and deep-rooted issues, experts believe.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is about 212GB, and thankfully, preloading is already underway. The game unlocks on November 19 at midnight local time, and that means US players will be among the last in the world to get in.

People in New Zealand, meanwhile, will be the first in the world to play GTA 6. If you're thinking about booking a flight to the land of Hobbits, here are some tips for packing your PS5 safely.

title: Xbox Project Helix Is A Console That Plays PC Games, Not The Other Way Around
text:
Xbox has revealed more details about its next-gen device, Project Helix, describing it as a "console capable of playing games from your PC."

Prominently featured in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, VP of next-gen Jason Ronald said the Xbox Series X|S successor is designed to build on the successes — and hard lessons — of previous Xbox generations, with fewer barriers to play.  "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine--one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed," Ronald said. "My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."

Ronald added that the Project Helix family of devices isn't purely focused on traditional next-gen themes like better graphics, but on thinking ahead to create "innovative" experiences. "We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K, or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics--it's really about gameplay innovation," Ronald explained. "We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Project Helix will also let "hardcore" gamers customize their gaming experience, but how much will all of this cost? Xbox isn't revealing a ballpark figure for Project Helix yet, but Ronald did mention the company is aiming to balance state-of-the-art gaming with an "affordable" price tag. Game preservation will also play a key role, letting users bring their Xbox library with them, and Ronald teased Project Helix as a brand that spans multiple facets of gaming, from living room experiences to handheld sessions and cloud streaming. As a sign of things to come, the Xbox mode on the recently released ROG Xbox Ally was mentioned as the direction the gaming division is headed.

The news on Project Helix comes at a time when Xbox has had several highs and lows throughout 2026. This year saw several first-party games release and earn plenty of acclaim, while the anniversary celebrations included a special-edition Xbox Series X that few people could get their hands on — for retail price, that is. At the same time, the rise of Asha Sharma as Xbox CEO has seen scores of jobs and studios slashed from the Xbox family as the company undergoes a "reset" aimed at making it more profitable.

title: GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects
text:
After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. The game is poised to "blot out the sun," some experts believe, and its release looms so large that other gaming companies are shifting dates for their own games to stay out of the blast radius. 

Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play. 

To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics.

He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself."

Spiegel said he foresees potential shifts beyond gaming, in places like TV viewership, music consumption, social media engagement, and even travel. "In an increasingly fragmented entertainment landscape, it's rare for a single release to command this much attention across so many industries simultaneously. That's what makes this moment so significant," he said.

An economics professor recently claimed that about 1.5 million people plan to "call out sick" to play GTA 6, and this could come at a "cost" of $1 billion to the US economy. Spiegel said people should remember that GTA 6 isn't anything new or special as it relates to taking time off work. "People regularly plan time off around major cultural and entertainment events, and this is another example of consumers prioritizing an experience they're excited about," he said.

That being said, Spiegel remarked that PwC has observed estimates suggesting time-off requests near GTA 6's release could be 9% to 17% higher than normal. "But what's more interesting to me is what happens outside the workplace. If millions of people are spending additional hours gaming, they're potentially spending less time watching television, going out to restaurants, or engaging in other activities," he said.

"And unlike a sporting event that lasts a few hours or a few weeks, this experience could keep people engaged for months. So the broader economic implications may extend well beyond a single day of missed work," he added.

"Huge net positive"

GTA 6 is expected to be an enormous success commercially--it's reportedly already sold 11 million units through pre-purchases, and that could rise to 25 million at launch. That would work out to $2 billion in revenue, which would cover the game's entire development budget and most of its marketing spend, Sensor Tower said. But many are also saying that GTA 6 represents the last of a dying breed, and that other publishers might learn all the wrong lessons from its success. Spiegel said GTA 6 is going to be a "huge net positive for the gaming industry as a whole," in part because its success will reiterate to the broader entertainment and media landscape that games are culturally significant. At the same time, Spiegel said he doesn't foresee a world in which other publishers try to replicate a blockbuster of this magnitude. 

"Very few organizations have the capital, expertise, and intellectual property required to support investments on this scale. These are extraordinary events, not necessarily repeatable business models," Spiegel said. 

If GTA 6 is the huge success it's projected to be, it could positively uplift the broader gaming ecosystem in a lot of ways, Spiegel continued. 

"It could attract new audiences, renew investor interest, and create opportunities across advertising, payments, technology, and content creation. The real lesson isn't that everyone needs to build the next billion-dollar game. It's that gaming is an increasingly powerful part of the entertainment economy, with opportunities that extend well beyond the games themselves," he said.

Some companies, like Ubisoft, see GTA 6 not as something to be strictly afraid of. CEO Yves Guillemot says, that's because the rising tide that is GTA 6 could help drive more people to gaming overall. In fact, Ubisoft is putting out a big new update for one of its biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, right around GTA 6's launch.

Mat Piscatella of Circana reminded people that not everyone wants to play GTA 6, and he pushed back against the theory that it's a bad business idea to launch a game near GTA 6.

"The fear of many teams to put their game in the same window as GTA is completely overblown. GTA is going to be a massive game. Of course it is. It’s going to be a huge cultural event, but not every one of the 49 million people who own a PS5 or an Xbox Series in the US is going to be interested in that," he told GamesBeat.

Could GTA 6 lead the push to more in-game ads?

Spiegel went on to say that one additional follow-on effect from GTA 6 could be something that gamers might balk at but publishers and investors might salivate over. He said that if GTA 6 succeeds in the way people expect it to, and draw people into its world for tens--or even hundreds--of hours, that could demonstrate to the wider market that it's time for gaming, as an industry, to do more with advertising. 

"When millions of people are spending substantial amounts of time in interactive entertainment environments, it's natural for advertisers and investors to consider how they might participate," he said. 

Advertising for mobile and social games is already commonplace, but it's less present in the PC and console gaming market. There are examples, of course, as companies have already undertaken efforts to put ads into gaming with mixed results. Gamers quickly revolted when EA put ads in a UFC game, prompting EA to pull them quickly to help quell the backlash. Despite that, EA recently announced the formation of a new EA Advertising division that will seek to put ads "directly into gameplay." That announcement didn't go over well, either, as fans pushed back against the idea of having to see ads in yet another place in their life. Other examples have been received more positively, or at least ambivalently, with a trucking company buying ad space in the American Truck Simulator series to help recruit staff. 

Xbox, for its part, has big plans to put more ads in gaming. Xbox CSO Matthew Ball said advertising in console games could help with the "two-sided problem" that AAA gaming faces today. Development costs keep going up and up, and Ball said ads--as long as they're not overly in-your-face--could be a way to help developers make more money and solidify their business fundamentals. Of course, if these companies insert more ads into gaming, that doesn't mean they'll stop hawking things like DLC, microtransactions, and battle passes; they'll likely both happen in concert. As Spiegel sees it, though, if executed correctly, advertising could be a big boon for gaming.

"What's particularly interesting is that the opportunity extends beyond placing advertisements inside games. There's an entire ecosystem of digital advertising infrastructure, technology, and services that could benefit as gaming continues to grow. I expect we'll see increasing interest in those opportunities, particularly from investors looking for exposure to gaming without taking on the considerable financial risks associated with developing blockbuster titles," he said.

More investment

During the COVID years, the gaming industry saw massive revenue and player growth as people, forced to stay inside due to stay-at-home orders, turned to games to pass the time, have fun, and connect with friends. At the same time, interest rates were historically low. The cost to borrow money was so attractive that publishers ramped up significantly. 

The COVID-era boost to gaming did not last, though, and the industry is now challenged, to say the least, with numerous developers cutting staff, cancelling projects, and scaling back in other ways. If GTA 6 is indeed a massive success, it could trigger renewed interest in gaming as an investment vehicle, Spiegel believes, but not necessarily exclusively for funding new games and studios. Instead, Spiegel said he foresees big investment growth for discrete elements of gaming, including advertising, payment services, and AI buildouts.

"I absolutely think a release of this magnitude will get the attention of investors, corporate executives, and private equity firms. But I don't necessarily think that translates into another wave of billion-dollar game development," he said. "The economics of producing games at this scale are incredibly challenging, and very few organizations have the resources, expertise, and intellectual property necessary to justify those investments."

"Instead, I think investors will increasingly ask how they can participate in the broader gaming ecosystem," Spiegel added. "That could mean opportunities in advertising, payment infrastructure, technology services, mobile gaming, or artificial intelligence applications that support game development."

On the subject of AI, Spiegel said he believes it's a "particularly interesting variable" because it could, at least in theory, allow developers to work more efficiently and bring down costs. There is debate about whether or not this is a genuine reality or wishful thinking on the part of AI companies trying to sell their products and services. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, for example, recently told Business Insider that, despite Take-Two adopting AI products for some of its workflows, the company has not seen a material decrease in its cost structure. In fact, many theorize that AI-supported workflows will only make work more intense. For his part, Spiegel said AI in game development remains only an "emerging opportunity rather than a guaranteed outcome."

"The longer-term impact may be less about creating another generation of massive blockbusters and more about directing investment toward the businesses and technologies that support the gaming economy," he said. 

Who should be afraid?

A lot has already been said and written about publishers moving their release dates to avoid GTA 6, and Spiegel said he foresees dramatic possibilities for how GTA 6 could take the wind out of the sails of other entertainment near its launch. He said GTA 6 is not just a major gaming launch. Instead, he thinks it's an "event that could temporarily reshape how millions of consumers spend their time and money."

"Streaming could be particularly vulnerable. Every hour someone spends gaming is potentially an hour they're not watching a television show or movie. And because this launch falls just before the holiday season, it could make it difficult for streaming services to match the exceptionally strong viewership numbers we saw last year," he said.

Movie theaters could be tested, Spiegel said, and one highly anticipated film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, will be one to watch in particular. It comes to theaters on Friday, November 20, which is one day after GTA 6 releases. Director Francis Lawrence said he hopes fans find the time to play GTA 6 and go see his movie, but it remains to be seen what effect, if any, GTA 6's release will have on that film's performance at the box office. Spiegel said movie studios are banking on the belief that the theatrical experience "offers something consumers can't get from their living rooms." 

There is a Thursday Night Football game happening on the same day that GTA 6 releases, with the Indianapolis Colts taking on the Houston Texans. Spiegel said the live-sports category overall could be "more resilient" because of its nature as an event happening live that fans of those teams, or fans of the NFL in general, feel compelled to watch live as it happens. A movie or TV show, meanwhile, is on-demand entertainment. 

GTA 6 is a hugely anticipated release, and it's poised to bring lapsed gamers back into the fold, but anyone who doesn't already have a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S should prepare themselves for sticker shock. That's because, for a variety of reasons, new consoles today are actually hundreds of dollars more expensive than they were when they launched in 2020.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has frankly acknowledged, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't shaking in his boots about what this means for GTA 6. He thinks GTA 6 will be so good and so compelling that people will buy in no matter what.

"I don’t think it will slow us down any because, you know, we’re delivering, we believe we’re delivering experiences that people want,” Zelnick said. “However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands."

Who benefits?

In terms of companies, products, people, and services that could benefit from the ripple effects of GTA 6's release, Spiegel said music associated with the game could surge in listening activity. This has already happened, as streams of Tom Petty's "Love Is A Long Road" surged after the first trailer for GTA 6 used the song back in 2023. More recently, Cliff Richard's 1976 hit "Devil Woman" showed up in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, helping the song reach more people, including young people who maybe never even knew about the song. Spiegel said social media platforms could benefit from GTA 6's release as well, thanks to fans uploading gameplay clips, livestreams, and other forms of user-generated content inspired by GTA 6. Beyond this, the world of food delivery could see an uptick in activity as people opt to stay in to play GTA 6 (while in-person restaurants and other nightlife venues could take a hit). 

"The broader point is that the impact could extend into parts of the economy we don't traditionally associate with gaming," Spiegel said. "For business leaders, the question is whether they're competing with this cultural moment for consumer attention or finding ways to participate in it. That's what makes this launch so much more interesting than simply tracking how many copies are sold."

title: “Physical” GTA 6 Copies Might Be Vulnerable To A Very Stupid But Serious Trick
text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight.

As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse.

In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6.

At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response.

If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: GTA 6 Owner Take-Two Is Not Interested In Selling Itself After EA Goes Private For $55 Billion
text:
Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says.

Speaking to David Rubenstein, Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company."

He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it.

"We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said.

Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops.

"But once you're over a billion dollars in annual revenue, and we're way beyond that point. Our guidance is $8 billion to $8.2 billion this fiscal year, additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed."

In early 2008, Electronic Arts privately pursued a buyout of Take-Two, but after the GTA and BioShock company rejected it, EA went public in an attempt to get a deal done. Later that year, EA abandoned its plans to try to buy Take-Two after the GTA company said it was worth more and EA refused to increase its bid.

In 2019, it was rumored that Sony was attempting to buy Take-Two, but that was ultimately deemed to be unconfirmed market chatter and not a formal bid.

Take-Two has a market cap of more than $42 billion, and that is expected to grow in the year ahead, so it would seemingly take a lot of money to convince Take-Two to sell. Going forward, Zelnick has teased that new GTA games could release even faster, and that could be a positive for the company's financials.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, and that's good news because the game has a massive file size.

title: GTA 6 Could Sell 55 Million Copies By Early Next Year, Report Says, And Average Selling Price Could Be $90
text:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success, but just how big will the launch be? Investor's Business Daily compiled data from a series of analyst reports about the game and its owner, Take-Two, and the consensus is that it's going to be a juggernaut.

In terms of sales, Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets said GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. He said the game could sell 45 million units alone during the game's launch quarter, which is well ahead of the estimates of 34.2 million that IBD compiled.

 "This is an outlier in every respect," Circana's Mat Piscatella told the publication. "There have been some big game launches in the past, but nothing quite at this scale, not only in terms of the investment, but in terms of the anticipation. It's in its own league."

GTA 6 is launching with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok said he's forecasting 50 million unit sales for the fiscal year 2027, and that the blended average selling price will be close to $90. According to Sensor Tower, early data suggested preorders were skewing toward the $100 edition, but by launch, it could be around 50/50.

Matthew Cost of Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, said if GTA 6 does indeed have strong sales out of the gate, this could create a "large potential audience" for the next iteration of GTA Online. Rockstar has not said anything yet about an online mode for GTA 6, but given the huge success of GTA Online for GTA 5, it's all but guaranteed that GTA 6 will incorporate online multiplayer as well.

Cost said this is a big deal for investors and may represent "the next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock price. Take-Two's share price is down about 10% so far in 2026, and currently trades around $228/share..

A new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 would no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways to spend more money, and that could be frustrating for fans but great news for investors who want to see bigger returns.

D.A. Davidson analyst Wyatt Swanson said Take-Two's share price could surge to $300 in part because he believes Rockstar will release a PC edition of GTA 6 and usher in GTA Online 2.0. These releases would "enable structurally higher margins" for Take-Two, he said.

According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has already sold 12 million copies and generated $1.2 billion in revenue. GTA 5, meanwhile, took 72 hours to clear $1 billion in revenue--GTA 6 reached that a week before release, apparently.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

title: You Can Probably Guess WoW: Forever’s Most Popular Race, Class, And Faction
text:
World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our teeth into as they relate to the most popular races, classes, and faction in the latest version of developer Blizzard's MMORPG.

Forever launched November 4, becoming the biggest launch in WoW history by concurrent and returning players. Aside from that fact, Blizzard hasn't shared additional information on exactly how many characters have been made or what classes are most popular.

For that, we turn to Raider.IO, a WoW stat-tracking website more commonly used in the modern version of the game to provide rankings and details related to raids and Mythic+ progression. 

According to the site, close to 3.9 million characters have been created across all regions and rulesets so far. Around 48% of those characters are on the Alliance, with nearly 52% being on the Horde.

The most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they currently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde.

It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo.

Skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. Consdiering how popular blood elves are in other versions of the game, the number of Skyborne feels low by comparison, though the fact they cost $30 to access probably has something to do with that.

As for what rulesets are most popular, the normal (PvE) server is far and away the biggest, with over 2 million characters. The PvP ruleset isn't too far behind with around 1.5 million characters. Those two rulesets dwarf the size of the game's two RP rulesets, which combined have around 250,000 players. 

With the exception of standard RP, every ruleset has a larger Horde population, a subject Blizzard recently commented on officially. In a forum post, Blizzard announced its goal is for PvP servers to be as close to 50/50 faction balance as possible, and would be placing restrictions on creating Horde characters on PvP rulesets in an effort to make that a reality.

"World of Warcraft: Forever's PvP is at its best when the Alliance and Horde are on equal footing, and we are dedicated to helping maintain that balance so that we can all witness battles at the epic scale that has made WoW: Forever PvP so memorable thus far," Blizzard said.  

One week after WoW: Forever's shockingly smooth launch, we've been impressed how visual updates and Blizzard's changes to the classic WoW formula have made the MMO feel brand new again. Forever received its first major class and dungeon changes earlier this week.

title: Official Zelda Website Raises Eyebrows By Labeling 3DS Game As Playable On Switch
text:
Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game.

A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site.

Currently, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter.

The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time (the original), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap.

If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service.

Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years."

title: GTA 6 And These Other Games Can Justify An $80 Price, Expert Says
text:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other big AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2, an outlier at $80?

According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott, $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples.

Elliott said that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices.

However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said.

"The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added.

Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports games could charge more, but that might be a tougher sell considering those games are full of microtransactions already.

"So not all games were created equal, and mid-tier AAA publishers--and also bigger publishers offering smaller games or remakes--will price downward at $40-$60," Elliott said.

There are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5.

At the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging, and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze.

New video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the company is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

title: GTA 6 In-Game TV Show Macca & Friends Looks Ridiculous In The Best Way
text:
Rockstar Games has released the first footage of an in-game GTA 6 TV show called "Macca & Friends," which is about a sunglass-wearing pink alligator and his wetland friends in Leonida (the stand-in for Florida).

One of Macca's friends is Pinchie the crab, who is Macca's landlord. Macca is also friends with a hat-wearing manatee and a flamingo. Check out the trailer below, which sets up a story where Macca needs to get money to pay his landlord. Macca & Friends will be available to watch on Weazel, which is GTA's version of Fox. For now, all we have is this teaser. Given Rockstar's extreme push toward depth and immersion, we wouldn't be surprised if Macca & Friends is an actual multi-episode TV show in GTA 6 that people can watch on their in-game couch.

GTA 6 has an impressive attention to detail, so much so that a lot of what Rockstar created, fans may never even see.

title: The PS5’s New Graphics-Upscaling Trick Is Spreading To More Games
text:
Sony has announced that several more games are getting a Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upgrade on PS5. Introduced in September, QSSR is an AI-guided upscaling technology similar to the PS5 Pro's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), and it originally supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei. That lineup is expanding over the next couple of weeks to include games like Control Resonant, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, The Finals, No Man's Sky, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.

While it's not quite as good as PSSR on the PS5 Pro, QSSR still does a noticeable job of adding detail and clarity without impacting performance. Sony added that since QSSR shares elements with PSSR, it makes games that support the PS5 Pro upscaling tech a "natural" fit for an upgrade on regular PS5 consoles.

Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is a good example, given Insomniac Games' familiarity with PSSR. The QSSR update is now available for the game, and Insomniac's head of technology, Mike Fitzgerald, said it'll apply to both Fidelity and Performance modes. For Control Resonant, Remedy Entertainment senior graphics programmer Erik Jansson said that QSSR will offer noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail, and the update will be available in December.

While there's no exact date for when Arc Raiders and The Finals will be updated, players can expect "increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements," according to Embarl Studios technical art director Mikael Linderholm. Hello Games founder Sean Murray said that the No Man's Sky QSSR update will be out in a "few weeks" and will see the game look sharper on PS5 while maintaining "the best possible" frame rate.

Finally, Paul Rustchynsky, game director at Expression Games, said that Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will also look cleaner and sharper on PS5 when the update is eventually available. If you're interested in seeing how different several of the games look with QSSR enabled, you can click the links below to see comparison videos:

  • Control Resonant
  • Arc Raiders
  • No Man's Sky
  • Hell Let Loose: Vietnam

The PS5 turns six years old later this month, and as of November 10, it has surpassed 100 million consoles sold. Ordinarily, all eyes would be on the next PlayStation generation at this point--which Sony says it is working on--and advances like QSSR may squeeze more life out of the PS5 before its successor arrives. Whatever form the next PlayStation takes, don't expect it to be cheap, as the current generation has gotten more expensive since 2020 and the PS6 could cost over $1,000. Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden recently touched on the topic, and he spoke about how true innovation from Sony would come in the form of cheaper hardware, not just better graphics.

title: Xbox Says Putting Ads In Games, Something No One Likes, Could Help Save Gaming
text:
Xbox Cloud Gaming now has a free ad-supported version that's rolling out as part of Microsoft's bigger push to bring more ads to Xbox. Jonathan Stringfield, who worked on Activision's advertising push and is now doing some of the same work in his title as GM for Xbox Media Solutions, said in an interview that people shouldn't see this as a move by Xbox to cram ads into all of its games.

“There is zero world where there is intention--written, explicit, implicit, or otherwise--that ads will be an option in all games. It might not even be the case on all features of the console, et cetera,” he told GamesBeat. “Where we want to have these integrated is places where it makes sense--where it can actually provide value in a positive way. Even if that means the total reach that we can have is going to be perhaps smaller than if we brute-forced it, that’s okay."

Stringfield went on to point out how the gaming industry today is at a crossroads if the existing model is to survive. Many are saying it won't, or shouldn't, but Stringfield said if it does, then companies either need to "dramatically increase the price of games" or "find other mechanisms" that allow companies to make more money and keep the business healthy.

Stringfield, whose job is to help sell ads, said ads could be a way forward.

“When we talk about advertising--and things that are adjacent to it that amount to recurrent revenue, whether it’s subscriptions or otherwise--what this allows for is an alternative," he said.

Xbox chief strategy officer, Matthew Ball, previously said Xbox's intention was not to "cram ads in everything."

“Ads should be used to offer more affordable alternatives alongside today’s ad-free experiences, in the hopes more could play as a result. Similar to how Netflix and Disney+ have ad tiers with all the same content, but at half the price or so,” he said. “At no point do I even mention in-game ads. I personally believe interrupting the gameplay experience would be bad.”

For Xbox Cloud Gaming, users can now stream their own games for free with ad-supported cloud gaming. Alternatively, people can purchase ad-free cloud playtime, or they can subscribe to Xbox Game Pass to get more time. However, starting this month, Xbox is putting hourly caps on how much people can stream before requiring them to pay more.

The ads on Xbox Cloud Gaming come in the form of pre-roll ads that people watch before getting into a game; they don't interrupt gameplay, however.

Video game prices have remained largely flat over the years, and this is part of the problem, some experts have said. Without price increases, the math just doesn't math when development costs and other expenses are factored in. For his part, Stringfield said price increases for games would not be "terribly popular," so he's looking at other systems, namely ads, to fill the gap.

The biggest game of 2026, Rockstar's GTA 6, costs $80 for its standard edition, scaling up to $100 for the Ultimate Edition and $400 for a collector's edition (which doesn't include the game). For comparison, GTA 5 launched in 2013 at $60--that same $60 is worth about $86 today after inflation. This is why Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick believes GTA 6 is a true bargain--it's "cheaper" than GTA 5 was some 13 years ago, he says.

But GTA 6 isn't the first game to charge $80--Nintendo ushered in this new era in 2025 with Mario Kart World.

People like former PlayStation executive Shawn Layden have said for years that companies refusing to raise prices was actually detrimental and has caused numerous systemic problems, contributing to the situation the industry finds itself in. Layden said the price of new games ought to have gone up $10 for each new console generation, and when that didn’t happen, companies made efforts to extract more money from people with things like microtransactions, battle passes, and subscriptions.

One Bank of America analyst believes the rest of the industry should follow Rockstar and start charging $80 for games. If more companies raise prices to $80 like Rockstar is doing with GTA 6, that doesn’t mean developers will stop hawking things like microtransactions, DLC, and battle passes. Instead, these efforts to increase ARPU will likely continue in concert with price hikes because why would a company cut off, or scale back, a revenue stream?

title: The Xbox 25th Anniversary Console Restock Sold Out Before You Could Finish Reading This Headline
text:
After quickly selling out earlier this year, Microsoft dropped a limited number of its 25th Anniversary Xbox Series X consoles for sale this week--aaaaannnd they're already gone. Easily the best-looking Xbox Series X console thanks to its transparent green case, it looks like the majority of people looking to get one of these are out of luck, unless they're willing to pony up and pay extra for one of these consoles on sites like eBay, where they're currently being listed at next-gen console prices.

Naturally, fans who missed out are livid, and online, they're calling out Xbox's first-come first-serve business model for selling the console, as opposed to a method like a lottery system that would even the playing field. Several disappointed buyers say that scalpers and bots go to all the remaining stock first, as they claim that it was sold out within seconds once again. People are especially mad at GameStop, as its dynamic pricing system had the console up for sale at the eye-watering price of $4,950, not including tax.

Over on eBay, beggars can't be choosers, as people continue to pay an inflated price for this Xbox Series X. Sales of it are averaging around $2,500 per console, a significant mark-up from the $900 MSRP of the device. In comparison, both Nintendo and Sony have implemented lottery and queue-based reservation systems in the past, specifically designed to thwart scalpers and filter out automated bots. Last year for the rollout of the Switch 2 in Japan, Nintendo utilized an official lottery system via the My Nintendo Store, which saw over 2 million people enter.

In western markets, Nintendo offered a direct invitation queue via regional Nintendo Accounts for verified active account holders. Sony's PS5 Pro has also become a hot item ahead of the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, and recently, Sony instituted an anti-scalping lottery system via the official Sony Store in Japan. To qualify for the draw, entrants were required to have a Japanese PlayStation Network account and a verified history of at least 60 hours of playtime on a PS4 or PS5 across the preceding two years.

But with Xbox hardware sales reaching historic lows recently? Microsoft probably isn't too worried about who buys its consoles, so long as it sells them.

title: Get Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater And All Bonus DLC Cheaper Than The Standard Edition Right Now
text:
I don’t think there’s ever been a more iconic sound than the ‘!’ noise that triggers when you’re spotted in Metal Gear Solid. Even when I was a little kid, my first exposure to the franchise was through the Mesal Gear Solid: Snake Escape minigame in Ape Escape 3. That’s not really relevant, besides the fact that it shares a similar name with Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater, a remake and an absolute blast that’s now cheaper than ever, with all DLC included.

If you ask anyone who has played the series, there’s a good chance that Snake Eater might be their favorite. Personally, I’m a sucker for The Phantom Pain and, of course, Metal Gear Rising—but a majority of fans love this one, and I can’t blame them. A prequel to the rest of the series, meaning it’s a perfect jumping-on point for interested newcomers, you play as Naked Snake, sent to Tselinoyarsk, USSR, to complete Operation: Virtuous Mission. But, like any secret mission, things go awry.

Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater is, narratively, the same game as the original, so fans shouldn’t expect anything too different from the 2004 version. Instead, the gameplay is fine-tuned with some quality-of-life changes, while keeping the stealth combat at its core the same. Just with a fresh coat of paint slapped on, of course.

And I’m really underselling it with the fresh coat of paint line. Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater completely refreshes the original, bringing it up to modern standards, with every element across the board brought to the current generation. Naked Snake has never looked so beautiful, and even one look at different screenshots for a direct comparison will show you just how overhauled the experience is.

In our Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater review, Tamoor said, while playing the game, “I wasn’t an adult yearning for the lost feelings that made me love Metal Gear Solid 3; I was the teenager living them for the first time again.” And, as an added bonus, that Ape Escape mission is still part of the Snake Eater experience. That’s purchase-worthy alone.

If you’re looking to play the game for the first time ever, or you’re hoping to relive your life two decades ago, you can grab the Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater Deluxe Edition for just $27.29 / £22.74 at Fanatical, getting you a Steam key with all of the bonus content at a lower price than Steam has ever offered the standard edition for. Not a bad way to celebrate November.

title: “You Guys Are F***ing Idiots”: Jeff Kaplan Takes Aim At Blizzard’s Overwatch 2 Reveal
text:
Saying Overwatch 2 has had a rocky road since its 2019 reveal would be an understatement, and former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan isn't a fan of how the game was first announced.

Speaking to Gaming World Interviews, Kaplan didn't mince words about the BlizzCon 2019 opening ceremony, where Overwatch 2 was shown for the first time, as Blizzard promised numerous features it either walked back or didn't deliver.

Kaplan said that from 2018 until his departure, he experienced constant friction with Blizzard's executive leadership over game direction, scheduling, and core game mechanics. This led him to confront leadership about the lack of a clear vision or business model for Overwatch 2, and to question the wisdom of announcing Overwatch 2 at the same time as Diablo 4.

"I got in a huge fight with, at the time, it wasn't Mike [Morhaime]. I loved Mike, who was the president of Blizzard, and another president of Blizzard, my executive producer, over announcing Overwatch 2. I went into their office, I’m like, 'What are we doing? We don’t really know what this game is; we don’t know what the business model is. This is a huge mistake.'"

According to Kaplan, the new executives "had a lot to prove" when they joined Blizzard. "They wanted to prove that 'Blizzard's back and Blizzard still has it.' And I'm like, 'You guys are f***ing idiots,' you know? I don’t know how else to put it, but after three years of just getting worn down and not agreeing with any of the decisions that were being made on the franchise and not feeling like I had agency anymore--like before it used to be like I'm the game director I get to decide the direction the game goes. And starting in 2018, I lost that, and after three years of fighting for it back, I realized this company belongs to these corporate people now, the Blizzard executive team, the Activision team."

Kaplan left Blizzard in 2021, saying Activision Blizzard’s financial arm told him that if Overwatch didn't meet certain financial goals, 1,000 people at the company would be laid off and the blame would fall on him. "The biggest f**k you moment I’ve had in my career--it felt surreal to be in that condition," Kaplan said earlier this year.

These days, Kaplan is working on The Legend of California at the new studio he co-founded, Kintsugiyama. The Blizzard veteran recently spoke to GameSpot about the "humbling" reality of being an indie dev and more.

title: Fable Is Looking A Lot Darker Than We Expected
text:
Amid a modest 25th-anniversary celebration, Xbox dropped a new preview of the Fable reboot. This snippet — which runs for under four minutes — offers plenty of gameplay and a closer look at some of the ghoulish enemies you'll face, set in a slice of Albion that looks surprisingly grim compared to the lighthearted Fable teasers that came before it.

"The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire," the video synopsis reads. "Here, they cross a threshold where the natural magic of Deepwood appears corrupted by an outside force, and they discover hints as to who or what could be responsible."

One thing to note about this snippet of gameplay is that it's pulled from the PC build of Fable, with the settings cranked up to Ultra. It's a pretty good-looking glimpse of what you can expect from Fable next year, even if it feels different from its cheekier predecessors and more like a feudal action slice reminiscent of Control Resonant toward the end, with its red-hued aesthetic.

Of course, four minutes of Fable doesn't tell the whole story, and with the main campaign alone estimated to take 20 hours to finish, that doom-and-gloom feeling probably won't be present throughout the entire game.

Fable launches February 23, 2027, for Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC, with Playground Games primarily handling development. Turn 10 Studios also assisted with development, and following recent changes at Xbox, it was merged into Playground Games.

In addition to Fable, Xbox also revealed that new Wolfenstein and Doom games are in development, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s open letter to the Xbox community suggested that future game development might be more reliant on AI.

title: Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In Production At MachineGames
text:
The long-rumored Wolfenstein 3 has been officially confirmed to be in development at MachineGames. The news follows many hints and rumors of a third game in MachineGames' planned Wolfenstein trilogy, the franchise's first new entry since Wolfenstein: Youngblood in 2019 and its first mainline title since 2017.

Xbox CEO Asha Shar posted the announcement as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations, and Bethesda also shared the news in its own post.

In a move borrowed from the film industry, the game announcement was accompanied by a look at Wolfenstein 3's script, showing that protagonist B.J. Blazkowicz is back and more fearsome than ever.

Bethesda also shared a photo from a mocap session, confirming that actors Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson will return to reprise their roles as B.J. and Grace Walker, respectively.

MachineGames has said that it always planned for a trilogy of Wolfenstein games featuring B.J., meaning Wolfenstein 3 will continue the story that started with The New Order in 2014.

MachineGames, alongside Bethesda, has also released three Wolfenstein spin-offs: the prequel The Old Blood in 2015, 2019's Youngblood, which featured B.J.'s twin daughters as protagonists, and the VR experience Cyberpilot, also released in 2019. The studio took a break from the Wolfenstein franchise to develop 2024's critically acclaimed Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

We don't have any more details on Wolfenstein 3 at present, including a release window, but we'll likely hear more soon.
